text: Elcmar is a figure of Irish mythology, often called a god or a hero. He is linked with the great monument Brú na Bóinne on the River Boyne. Legends name him the husband of Bóand, the river goddess also called Eithne. She took the Dagda as her lover and asked him to hold the sun still for nine months, so her pregnancy passed in a single day. Their son, Aonghus Óg, was born. The boy later tricked Elcmar out of the Brú so that he could make it his home. In some accounts the husband is named Nechtan or Nuada instead.
